reasoning: Dustin May has a 5.65 ERA in 10 appearances with Milwaukee and an 8.59 ERA over his final three regular-season starts, lasting 3 innings or fewer in each. He hasn't pitched in the postseason since 2020.
Nick Pivetta has a 1.64 ERA in five starts (22 IP, 4 BB) since coming back from the IL on Sept. 7. He allowed 1 run in 3.1 IP in the Wild Card clincher and has a 2.86 career postseason ERA.
San Diego went 53-30 at home this season, and Game 3 is at Petco Park.
Both Milwaukee wins were by one run (3-2, 4-3). San Diego's offense went 3-for-18 with runners in scoring position, which points to bad sequencing more than a real talent gap.
Market: Padres -134 to -136 across books (implied 57%). I estimate about 59%, an edge of roughly 2 points, so this is sized Low.
risks: May has dominated San Diego this year (1.23 ERA, 22 K in 22 IP over three starts), and Milwaukee is a deep, elite team (the NL Central leader), so its bullpen can cover a short May outing.
Pivetta is just back from a five-month elbow injury and may be on a short leash, which pushes more innings onto the Padres bullpen.
San Diego's offense has scored only 5 runs in two games and could keep stalling.

reasoning: Aaron Judge (right calf strain) is not on the ALDS roster, and the Yankees have scored just 2 runs across Games 1 and 2 (lost 1-0 and 5-2).
Tampa Bay went 31-17 against left-handed starters in the regular season, which blunts the main edge New York has with Max Fried on the mound.
Fried allowed 7 runs on 12 hits over 14.2 innings in two starts against Tampa Bay this season, despite a 2.80 ERA overall in 20 starts (he missed time on the IL).
Nick Martinez had a 3.10 ERA and 1.09 WHIP over 31 starts, with a 2.38 ERA in 16 road starts and 3 runs allowed in 12 innings at Yankee Stadium this year.
The Rays bullpen needed only about seven relief outs over the first two games, so it is fully rested for a short leash on Martinez.

Fried's partner is due to give birth this week; Carlos Rodon would move up if he is unavailable. Market range is +134 to +145 (implied about 42%); I estimate about 45%, an edge of roughly 3 points, sized Low.
risks: Fried is a true ace when right, and the Yankees ranked fourth in MLB in home wRC+ (111) and scored 18 runs in two home Wild Card games, so the offense could wake up back in the Bronx.
Martinez has allowed 6 runs over his last two starts and lost three of his last four outings.
This is a popular underdog side with many previews on it, so some of the value may already be priced in; a 3-point edge is thin.

reasoning: Parker Messick: 2.56 ERA, 3.07 FIP, 3.37 xFIP over 186.1 innings and 32 starts; 2 runs on 4 hits with 6 strikeouts in Game 1 of this series.
Messick has gone at least five innings in all four starts against Chicago this year, with eight strikeouts in three of them and a 2.45 ERA at Rate Field (18 K, 2 BB in 14.2 innings).
Before Game 3, the White Sox openers Hagen Smith and Grant Taylor had combined for 17 strikeouts and 1 earned run over 14 innings in the postseason; Cleveland scored only 3 runs in Games 1 and 2.
Game 3 had a postseason-record 19 combined strikeouts, and Chicago struck out 19 times on its own side of that.

Market: the under is about 52.8% fair after removing the margin (DraftKings 7.5 at -122, another listing at -113). At 1.87 that is a 1.4% expected loss, so it is sized at the 0.25u minimum and should only be taken at 1.92 or better.
risks: Both bullpens are stretched: Chicago's has worked extra innings three games in a row, and Cleveland used Griffin, Cantillo and closer Cade Smith for over six innings on Wednesday.
Cleveland just scored 9 runs in Game 3, including a bases-loaded triple off Smith, and these teams went over in 8 of their last 10 meetings.
The total is only priced at two sources, and the White Sox (776 runs) have far more power than Cleveland, so one big inning sinks it.
